H01.description: A dead build stage cargo-installs beads_rust 0.2.6, which the file itself says is not on crates.io, so a builder that builds every stage (the legacy builder) fails the image build.

H02.description: The pip dependencies use >= ranges and the bats-core clone trusts a movable tag, so a rebuild can pull different, unverified code into the image that is supposed to be reproducible.

H03.description: Header comment updated to describe the eval/-first envelope read and the arm grammar check.

H04.description: Header comment documents the new zone_violations fields.

H05.description: Header comment documents the extra --validate checks.

H06.description: Header comment documents the new exit-2 message and the file-based jq inputs.

H07.description: The --help line range is widened to cover the longer header.

H08.description: --validate never checks the arm against the arm grammar (and checks only one zone_violations array), so rows with a malformed arm pass validation.

H09.description: Inputs that grow with the run (grade, manifest, task, pipeline.json) are held in shell strings and later passed to jq as --argjson argv, so a large run goes over MAX_ARG_STRLEN and the row cannot be built.

H10.description: envelope() prefers the agent-writable sandbox copy of the dissent envelope over the harness eval/ copy, so a later phase can tamper with voices_run and degraded; the hunk also moves the MODELINV and manifest inputs to files and adds the arm grammar check.

H11.description: The transcript write list goes to a file instead of a shell variable, as part of the argv-limit fix.

H12.description: The row jq call passes every run-scaled input (MODELINV, pipeline.json, envelopes, writes) as --argjson argv strings, which fails on long runs past the per-argument limit; the hunk also hardens ms() and voices().

H13.description: A models_used that is not an object (e.g. an array) makes keys[] abort the whole row program.

H14.description: An empty or non-Z-offset started/finished timestamp makes ms()/fromdateiso8601 abort the row build; the hunk binds the guarded timestamps.

H15.description: A phase without name or model_requested, or with a non-object models_used, passes null or bad shapes into the row, which then fails validation.

H16.description: A non-boolean verdict_accuracy or a non-object verdict_accuracy_per_gate either aborts the row program or produces a row with the wrong field types.

H17.description: wall_clock_ms calls ms() on a present but unparseable started/finished and aborts, instead of falling back to the phase sum.

H18.description: zone_violations records only Write/Edit inputs under .claude/, so Bash rewrites of the mount and changed CLAUDE.md/.loa.config.yaml never show up; a failed row program also exits with a bare jq error.

H19.description: Header comment documents that the enforce variable is unset in every mode, the effort whitelist and the new executor.json field.

H20.description: The usage line range is widened to cover the longer header.

H21.description: An inherited LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE is unset only in arm mode, so the operator's gate override still reaches the baseline (non-arm) executor.

H22.description: Captures the enforce value at launch so executor.json can record it.

H23.description: The arm's effort toggle reaches the CLI argv without a low|medium|high|xhigh|max whitelist check in this script.

H24.description: Passes the recorded enforce value to the executor.json jq call.

H26.description: Header comment documents the --bats-bin default without the host fallback.

H27.description: When bats is not on PATH, the script falls back to a host-specific path under the operator's dotfiles and executes it, so the fingerprint depends on that one machine and runs an unexpected binary.

H28.description: Header comment documents the symlink and newline refusals.

H29.description: The usage line range is widened to cover the longer header.

H30.description: The manifest listing uses find -type f, so symlinks are silently left out (their targets can change the suite while the manifest stays the same), and a path holding a newline splits into two bogus listing entries.

H31.description: Header comment documents the once-per-gate envelope copy.

H32.description: Corrects the codex version named in a header comment.

H34.description: The --help line range is widened to cover the longer header.

H36.description: Adds the hashing and mount-integrity helper functions.

H37.description: Passes mount_integrity to the pipeline.json jq call.

H40.description: Computes mount integrity on an abnormal exit.

H41.description: No baseline hash of sandbox CLAUDE.md/.loa.config.yaml is taken after materialisation, so an agent that rewrites the mount through Bash leaves no record.

H42.description: Every phase copies every sandbox adversarial-*.json to eval/ and overwrites the earlier copy, so a later FIX/AUDIT phase that edits a gate's envelope replaces the harness evidence (symlinks are followed too).

H43.description: Passes the envelope copy fields to the phase-record jq call.

H44.description: Records envelope_copied and envelope_sha256 on gate phase records.

H45.description: Header comment documents the assumed-cap charge.

H46.description: Header comment documents marker-based screen exclusion.

H47.description: The usage line range is widened to cover the longer header.

H48.description: A regular --batch whose name starts with screen- is accepted, and then the suite aggregate silently drops it because it excludes batches by directory name.

H52.description: The aggregate does not filter on the STATUS.json screen marker, so a screen batch in a directory not named screen-* is counted in the suite totals and cuts.

H53.description: Screen batches are excluded by the screen-* directory path rather than by the marker, which drops regular batches with that prefix and keeps unmarked-name screen batches.

H54.description: A failed trial that reports no cost (killed, transport loss) adds 0 to spent, so the --max-usd cap underestimates real spend and launches too many trials.

H55.description: A trial that writes no row at all is charged nothing to spent, which also undercounts spend against the cap.

H56.description: Header comment documents dedup by larger cost and anonymous rows.

H57.description: Header comment documents the INCOMPLETE output and the exit 1.

H58.description: The usage line range is widened to cover the longer header.

H59.description: Dedup keeps the first-seen row of a run_id, so a run rowed twice (a smoke row, then the graded row) counts whichever cost came first rather than the larger one, which can undercount spend.

H60.description: A duplicate run_id is skipped once seen, so the counted cost depends on file and row order instead of being the larger cost.

H61.description: The JSON output does not mark a total that skipped malformed lines as incomplete (no complete flag).

H62.description: When malformed lines are skipped, the total is only a lower bound, yet the script prints it without an INCOMPLETE mark and exits 0.

H63.description: Header comment documents the envelope source order.

H64.description: The --help line range is widened to cover the longer header.

H65.description: took-effect's envelope() reads the agent-writable sandbox envelope before the harness eval/ copy, so a tampered sandbox envelope decides one_voice_planned.

H66.description: Test updated to edit the eval/ envelopes.

H67.description: Adds tests for envelopes, bash_mount_refs, mount_changed, validation and the arm grammar.

H68.description: Adds tests for a large MODELINV ledger, odd field shapes and a row abort.

H69.description: Fixes and extends the enforce-variable test.

H70.description: Stub documentation for the new tamper knobs.

H71.description: Stub implements the envelope-tamper and CLAUDE.md-append knobs.

H72.description: Adds the symlink and newline refusal tests.

H73.description: Adds the envelope-copy and mount-integrity tests.

H74.description: Adds the Dockerfile, header-version and fingerprint tests.

H75.description: Adds the screen-marker and assumed-cap tests.

H77.description: Test now expects exit 1 and complete false.

H78.description: Adds the INCOMPLETE, larger-cost dedup and anonymous-row tests.

H79.description: Adds the test that the eval/ envelope is read first.

I01.description: The per-run container HOME gets a full copy of the host ~/.codex/auth.json, refresh token included, so containers consume the host refresh token and the host and later containers lose Codex auth.

I02.description: Grader contamination-heuristic false positives in ablation-grade.sh; not shown in this change's head code.

I03.description: A mount-design hazard for review-catch tasks (later framework copy exposed), found in a later analysis; nothing in the head text shown points to a specific defect.

I04.description: Concerns the overlay_answer_paths closed mount, which cycle-131 added later.

I05.description: A model refusal fallback is designed behaviour, correctly flagged as degraded; not a defect.

I06.description: The eval_only/oracle_open handling was a cycle-131 feature added after this change.

I07.description: Type checking of oracle_open, a cycle-131 toggle added later.

I08.description: A later pull request description, not a defect report.
